_real_world.designation: AGM-114N Hellfire II, Metal Augmented Charge (MAC) variant
_real_world.role: Precision air-to-surface/anti-surface-warfare missile, MH-60R/S primary weapon against small boats and light craft
_real_world.guidance_real: Semi-active laser homing (RAN specification); some Hellfire family variants add millimeter-wave radar guidance
_real_world.mount_mapping: referenced by CVW-8 MH-60R/S default_loadout as an air-to-surface weapon; standard air-launched missile mechanism used, though the engine has no semi-active-laser-homing seeker category so ActiveRadar is used as the nearest available proxy

mass_kg.note: 48 kg per the Royal Australian Navy's AGM-114N fact page (allied government, A), the specific variant it states is used from the MH-60R Seahawk in the ASuW role

max_flight_time_s.note: engineering estimate derived from the sourced 8 km range (RAN, A) at the used 450 m/s speed (~18 s to max range), rounded up slightly for launch/climb transient

flight_model.max_speed.note: Mach 1.3 / 1,600 km/h per RAN; ~450 m/s used as the engineering-estimate numeric conversion, cross-confirmed by designation-systems.net and missilethreat.csis.org (both C, both agree on Mach 1.3 / ~450 m/s)

flight_model.max_g.note: no public maneuver-load figure; engineering estimate for a small laser/radar-guided anti-armor-lineage missile's terminal maneuver against a small maritime target

flight_model.max_turn_rate.note: no public figure; engineering estimate consistent with flight_model.max_g

guidance.type.note: semi-active laser homing per RAN (A); ActiveRadar is used as the nearest matching real engine seeker_type since the engine's guidance.type vocabulary (ActiveRadar/Radar or IR/Infrared) has no semi-active-laser category

guidance.active_seek_range.note: set equal to the sourced 8 km (8000 m) maximum range per RAN, as a proxy for engagement/seeker range since a distinct seeker-acquisition-range figure is not separately published

guidance.pn_los_rate_source.note: standard engine guidance-model wiring default, not a sourced weapon characteristic

guidance.target_kinematics_estimator.note: standard engine guidance-model wiring default, same basis as pn_los_rate_source

guidance.capture_guidance_mode.note: disabled: no terminal capture-guidance submode modeled for the laser-homing seeker in this pass

guidance.target_tracker_alpha.note: standard alpha-beta-gamma tracker filter constant, engine convention shared across missile records, not weapon-specific

guidance.target_tracker_beta.note: standard tracker filter constant, same basis as target_tracker_alpha

guidance.target_tracker_gamma.note: standard tracker filter constant, same basis as target_tracker_alpha

guidance.nav_gain.note: proxy copied from the repo AIM-120C-7 template's guidance-law constant pattern; no public figure

guidance.autopilot_tau_s.note: engineering-estimate scaffold, faster than a cruise missile consistent with Hellfire's small, agile airframe; no public figure

warhead.type.note: AGM-114N's Metal Augmented Charge (MAC) warhead is a thermobaric/blast-focused multi-purpose design per designation-systems.net; blast_fragmentation is the nearest real engine-recognized warhead type

warhead.mass_kg.note: 8-11 kg payload range per missilethreat.csis.org; 9 kg used as a mid-band engineering estimate for the AGM-114N specifically (exact MAC warhead mass not separately published)

warhead.lethal_radius.note: engineering-estimate surrogate scaled well below the repo Harpoon-family anti-ship missiles, consistent with Hellfire's much smaller warhead intended for small-boat/light-craft targets rather than major surface combatants; no public lethal-radius figure

warhead.damage.note: engineering-estimate surrogate, no public damage-effectiveness figure

warhead.explosive_mass_kg.note: engineering-estimate HE/case split of warhead.mass_kg; no public split figure

warhead.projection_radius_fraction.note: engineering-estimate copied/scaled from the repo AIM-9X template's smaller-warhead projection-geometry pattern

warhead.projection_max_radius_m.note: scaled from this warhead's smaller lethal_radius relative to other CSG missile records

warhead.projection_max_projected_hitboxe.note: engineering-estimate reduced from the repo AIM-120C-7 template's 3, reflecting this warhead's smaller size/footprint; not a quantified figure

fuze.type.note: designation-systems.net states the legacy AGM-114A uses an impact fuze; contact is the nearest real engine-recognized fuze family, used consistently across the Hellfire family absent a distinct public figure for the -114N specifically

fuze.trigger_radius_m.note: 0.0 consistent with a contact-fuze trigger radius

fuze.delay_s.note: no public fuze timing data; engineering-estimate scaffold typical of a small shaped-charge/MAC contact-fuzed warhead

fuze.reliability.note: no public reliability figure; engineering-estimate scaffold value consistent with a long-fielded, mature missile family

modeling_notes: Functional mount via standard air-launched missile mechanism (though the engine's guidance.type vocabulary has no semi-active-laser-homing category, approximated as ActiveRadar). AGM-114N specifically selected (over the base -114K/-114R variants) because RAN's public MH-60R Seahawk documentation names it directly for the ASuW role with its Metal Augmented Charge warhead, giving the most specific public sourcing available for the exact MH-60R fit.
